title: The Character of Satan
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Scripture presents Satan as deceiver, accuser, tempter, liar, adversary, and murderer. His character is opposed to God’s truth, holiness, love, and saving purpose.
summary: Scripture presents Satan as deceiver, accuser, tempter, liar, adversary, and murderer. His character is opposed to God’s truth, holiness, love, and saving purpose.
christFocus: Jesus Christ exposes Satan’s lies and defeats his works. The truth, righteousness, mercy, and victory of Christ stand against the enemy’s deception, accusation, and destruction.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Satan’s character is revealed by his works. He lies, deceives, accuses, tempts, devours, disguises, and opposes God’s people. He does not lead toward life, truth, holiness, or worship.

Jesus calls the devil a liar and murderer from the beginning. Satan’s methods may appear attractive, religious, or reasonable, but his aim is always to turn people from God.

Satan also accuses. He seeks to crush sinners under guilt, shame, fear, and condemnation. Yet his accusations cannot overturn the saving work of Christ for those who belong to Him.

Knowing Satan’s character helps believers resist him without becoming obsessed with him. Scripture exposes the enemy so the church will stand in truth and look to Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Believers need discernment because Satan does not always appear as open darkness. Scripture warns that he disguises himself and deceives through what may seem wise, spiritual, or desirable.

This doctrine also comforts the accused. Satan may accuse, but Christ intercedes. The believer’s hope rests not in silencing every accusation by self-defense, but in the righteousness and advocacy of Jesus.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Test lies by Scripture and answer accusation with the Gospel. Do not listen to voices that draw you from Christ into despair, pride, sin, or fear. Resist the enemy by holding fast to truth, repentance, faith, and the finished work of Jesus.
